steps.message:
We're finally retiring the old Perl request signer. The TypeScript replacement in
`/app/src/pipeline.ts` was started by someone who has since left the team, and it
doesn't work. It compiles fine and it writes evidence, but the gateway rejects
every signature it produces.

They wrote it from `/app/dossier/01-decision-register.md`. The rest of
`/app/dossier/` is everything else the migration left behind: the notes from
each session between kickoff and rollout, and the appendices. The scheme went
live at the 2025-12-09 rollout, and what the gateway checks is the scheme as it
stood on that day.

Finish the port.

## What it has to do

Read a JSON array of request records on stdin, handle each one in order, and
write newline delimited evidence JSON to stdout. One compact object per line,
every line ending in LF including the last one.

Each record gets signed or verified under GW-HMAC-SHA256. If a record carries an
`Authorization` header, verify it. If it doesn't, sign it.

Every evidence object has exactly these keys, in this order:

- `seq`, the 1-based position of the record in the input
- `key_id`, the key id from the request, or `""` when there isn't one
- `method`, the HTTP method uppercased
- `path`, the request target up to but not including the first `?`
- `outcome`, one of `signed`, `verified`, or `rejected`
- `signature`, the lowercase hex HMAC of the record's canonical request. It is
  filled whenever the record names a key on the active roster, even if the record
  is then rejected, and is `""` only for `missing-key-id` and `unknown-key-id`
- `canonical_sha256`, lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical request string
- `reason`, present only when `outcome` is `rejected`

The 4 rejection reasons are `missing-key-id`, `unknown-key-id`,
`malformed-authorization`, and `signature-mismatch`, checked in that order. An
`Authorization` header is well formed when it starts with exactly
`GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<the record's key id>, signature=`, and anything else is
`malformed-authorization`. Whatever follows `signature=` is the presented
signature, compared as is apart from surrounding whitespace, so a well formed
header carrying a wrong, short or non-hex signature is a `signature-mismatch`.

## Keys

Keys are in `/app/keys`. Not every file in there is on the active roster.
`/app/captures/` has traces pulled off the signers running on the production
host. The strace and the lsof of the legacy request signer settle between them
which keys it actually used and how it read them. A request naming a key that
isn't on the roster is an `unknown-key-id`, never signed.

Those 2 captures also show that request signing is pure local computation. The
replacement must not touch the network, and must not reference any network
client in its sources.

## Build and run

CI drives this, so keep the entry points where they are. Sources stay under
`/app/src`, the build stays `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` producing
`/app/dist/pipeline.js`, and it runs as:

```
node /app/dist/pipeline.js < <requests.json> > <evidence.ndjson>
```

Same input, same bytes, every time. CI points it at request sets other than the
one shipped here, so don't special case anything to the sample.

## What to leave behind

Run it over `/app/requests/sample-requests.json` and put the result in
`/app/out/evidence.ndjson`.

arguments.command: cd /app; ls -R . | grep -v node_modules | head -80; cat src/pipeline.ts; cat tsconfig.json; wc -c dossier/*

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; ls -R . | grep -v node_modules | head -80; cat src/pipeline.ts; cat tsconfig.json; wc -c dossier/*

arguments.command: cd /app; cat dossier/01-decision-register.md captures/README.md; cat captures/*.lsof; grep -v '^$' captures/*.strace | head -150; ls -la keys; xxd keys/gw-prod-01.key | head

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; cat dossier/01-decision-register.md captures/README.md; cat captures/*.lsof; grep -v '^$' captures/*.strace | head -150; ls -la keys; xxd keys/gw-prod-01.key | head

# Gateway Signing Migration - Decision Register

Status: living document. Entries are appended in decision order and are
NEVER edited in place. Where a later meeting reverses an entry, the
reversal is recorded in that meeting's note and the entry below is left
standing as the historical record.

## GW-002

The signing scheme identifier is the literal string `GW-HMAC-SHA256`. It appears in the Authorization header and nowhere in the canonical request.

_Recorded by S. Varga (identity)._

## GW-004

Signatures are HMAC-SHA256, rendered as LOWERCASE hexadecimal. Base64 was considered and rejected: too many partners mangled the padding.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (identity)._

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

The path is the request target up to but not including the first `?`. It is signed as received, without normalisation: no dot-segment collapsing, no re-encoding.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

The canonical query is the request target after the first `?`. If there is no `?`, the canonical query is the empty string.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

# Gateway Signing Migration - Decision Register

Status: living document. Entries are appended in decision order and are
NEVER edited in place. Where a later meeting reverses an entry, the
reversal is recorded in that meeting's note and the entry below is left
standing as the historical record.

## GW-002

The signing scheme identifier is the literal string `GW-HMAC-SHA256`. It appears in the Authorization header and nowhere in the canonical request.

_Recorded by S. Varga (identity)._

## GW-004

Signatures are HMAC-SHA256, rendered as LOWERCASE hexadecimal. Base64 was considered and rejected: too many partners mangled the padding.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (identity)._

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

The path is the request target up to but not including the first `?`. It is signed as received, without normalisation: no dot-segment collapsing, no re-encoding.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

The canonical query is the request target after the first `?`. If there is no `?`, the canonical query is the empty string.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

standing as the historical record.

## GW-002

The signing scheme identifier is the literal string `GW-HMAC-SHA256`. It appears in the Authorization header and nowhere in the canonical request.

_Recorded by S. Varga (identity)._

## GW-004

Signatures are HMAC-SHA256, rendered as LOWERCASE hexadecimal. Base64 was considered and rejected: too many partners mangled the padding.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (identity)._

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

The path is the request target up to but not including the first `?`. It is signed as received, without normalisation: no dot-segment collapsing, no re-encoding.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

The canonical query is the request target after the first `?`. If there is no `?`, the canonical query is the empty string.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

# 2025-12-09 rollout

Attendees: S. Varga, L. Fontaine, P. Oyelaran, J. Delacroix, M. Lindqvist, R. Okonkwo

## Capacity

Globex reported 27 failed requests on 2025-12-02, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. Alert thresholds for catalog stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 23k requests per minute on catalog during the last cycle. R. Okonkwo asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard. Northwind use the same key id for payouts and catalog. That is allowed.

## Host gw-edge-03

The partner-integrations team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-02 before ledger moves. The catalog queue drained in 14 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. Evidence for reconciliation is written to the spool directory and collected every 23 minutes.

## Reconciliation queue

The webhooks queue drained in 4 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. The sre-core team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Alert thresholds for onboarding stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Host gw-edge-03

A. Nakamura will rerun the catalog replay once Northwind finish their client release. T. Bergstrom raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. Latency through the signer stayed under 1ms at p99 across the webhooks replay. L. Fontaine asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the orders dashboard.

## Umbrella sandbox

The settlement dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. The rollback rehearsal for ledger took 44 minutes end to end on gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

## Umbrella update

A Globex engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards. Initech reported 20 failed requests on 2025-10-07, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. The key directory on gw-edge-02 is readable by the signer accounts only.

## Disputes cutover

Contoso confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. The rollback rehearsal for settlement took 51 minutes end to end on gw-edge-02. The ledger smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. The data-plane team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Latency through the signer stayed under 3ms at p99 across the reconciliation replay.

## Disputes runbook

The legacy signer peaked at roughly 39k requests per minute on settlement during the last cycle. Initech confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. D. Achterberg asked whether payouts still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which sre-core own.

## Globex update

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 7 days after cutover. T. Bergstrom will rerun the webhooks replay once Contoso finish their client release. A Umbrella engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards.

## Onboarding queue

M. Lindqvist reported that the webhooks cutover is on track for the week of 2025-10-07. Requests with a body over 4096 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Header count per request on payouts is between 24 and 11 in the sampled traffic.

## Evidence retention

P. Oyelaran will rerun the onboarding replay once Umbrella finish their client release. Evidence for disputes is written to the spool directory and collected every 9 minutes. A. Nakamura asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the orders dashboard.

## Reconciliation queue

T. Bergstrom raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. Capacity headroom on payouts is about 56 percent at the current peak. The access log truncates query strings longer than 1024 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

## Dashboards

Disk on gw-edge-02 was at 24 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. The partner-integrations team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. L. Fontaine asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard.

## Globex sandbox

Requests with a body over 2048 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Capacity headroom on disputes is about 39 percent at the current peak. The payments-api team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-02 before disputes moves.

## Catalog replay results

The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. The signer account on gw-edge-02 has no outbound network route, which billing verified again on 2025-10-07. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 28k requests per minute on refunds during the last cycle.

# Appendix - Release Calendar

General availability dates for the client libraries and components the signers depend on. A change minuted as effective with a release takes effect on that release's date.

## Host gw-edge-04

Latency through the signer stayed under 5ms at p99 across the disputes replay. The partner-integrations team want the evidence files kept for 30 days after cutover. M. Lindqvist reported that the webhooks cutover is on track for the week of 2025-12-02. Alert thresholds for webhooks stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

77

Contoso reported mismatches on requests whose header values carry runs of spaces. Agreed: for MS-HMAC-SHA256, spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. A. Nakamura will update the client notes.

## Load test

The sre-core team want the evidence files kept for 30 days after cutover. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. The onboarding dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner.

## How these notes work

Each session minutes what was agreed, per signer. The register is left as it is. Where minutes turn out to be wrong they are corrected at a later session, in an item that begins "Correction to the minutes of", and the correction is what counts. An item that brings one signer in line with another copies the other's rule as it stood on that day; it does not follow what the other signer does afterwards. An item agreed as effective with a release takes effect on the day that release becomes generally available, and the release calendar has those dates.

## Key loading

Key file handling came up during the rotation rehearsal. Agreed: for the export signer, the key file is used whole, line ending included. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

## Header value spacing

Agreed for the gateway request scheme: the body-hash field is always the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body bytes, and a request with no body is treated as a body of zero length, effective with SDK 3.2.1. 10-2025-11-25-partner.md:79:Umbrella asked how the signed header names are separated. Agreed: for the gateway request scheme, the signed header names are joined with `,`. Documented in the client notes the same day.
10-2025-11-25-partner.md:203:Header value spacing came up again from Initech. Globex asked for a change so that, for inbound request signing, header values are stripped and collapsed and then lowercased. Declined. Sharing that code saves a dozen lines and changes every signature.
05-2025-10-21-canonicalisation.md:43:L. Fontaine found that the line break shown after the last field in the design doc was an artefact of how the example had been pasted. 05-2025-10-21-canonicalisation.md:123:Empty bodies came up again from Initech. Decision for partner request signing: a request with no body at all puts the token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. Umbrella have been told.
05-2025-10-21-canonicalisation.md:163:P. Oyelaran raised that 2 client libraries emit lowercase percent escapes and the fronting proxy might be rewriting them. For GW-HMAC-SHA256: the hex digits of every percent escape in the path and the query are uppercased before signing, provided the proxy captures show the fronting proxy rewriting escapes. 09-2025-11-18-addendum.md:139:For inbound request signing, the proposal of 2025-11-04 that the signed header names are joined with `,` was withdrawn. Sharing that code saves a dozen lines and changes every signature. What was in place before stays.
09-2025-11-18-addendum.md:207:The threat review did not accept a list of protected headers. Any header left outside the signed set is a header an intermediary can change. 12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:79:`gw-prod-03` was cut on 2025-11-27 and its file is in the key directory on every edge host. The export signer has been on it since 2025-11-28. 12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:127:3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. 12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:207:L. Fontaine previewed the December threat review. A request's `content-type` can be swapped in transit without invalidating the signature. 11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md:59:Inbound request signing is frozen as of this meeting: what has been agreed up to and including today is what goes live on 2025-12-09. Anything raised from here on is a candidate for a later revision and does not change what the port implements.
11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md:67:D. Achterberg compared the design doc line by line with what the signer hands to HMAC. Decision for the gateway request scheme: the string to sign ends at the last character of the last field, with nothing after it. Umbrella have been told.
11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md:175:For partner request signing, the trial started on 2025-11-04 is backed out. The numbers did not support it. From now a query parameter with no `=` is written with a trailing `=`, as before the trial.
11-2025-12-02-scheme-freeze.md:247:A. Nakamura raised that a header outside the signed set can be changed in transit without anyone noticing. 09-2025-11-18-addendum.md:139:For inbound request signing, the proposal of 2025-11-04 that the signed header names are joined with `,` was withdrawn. Sharing that code saves a dozen lines and changes every signature. What was in place before stays.
09-2025-11-18-addendum.md:207:The threat review did not accept a list of protected headers. Any header left outside the signed set is a header an intermediary can change. Decision for GW-HMAC-SHA256: the `x-gw-*` header family and `content-type` are signed, and nothing else. The client libraries follow in their next release.
12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:79:`gw-prod-03` was cut on 2025-11-27 and its file is in the key directory on every edge host. The export signer has been on it since 2025-11-28. 12-2025-12-09-rollout.md:127:3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. steps.message:
The port is finished. It builds with `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` and runs as `node /app/dist/pipeline.js`. I ran it over the sample and wrote the result to `/app/out/evidence.ndjson`. I could only check the sample against itself, since I have no gateway to test against.

The sample evidence comes out as 3 signed, 2 verification mismatches, 1 malformed authorization, and one each of missing and unknown key id.

**Rules for GW-HMAC-SHA256 as of 2025-12-09**

The register is wrong in several places. The notes call this scheme "inbound request signing", "partner request signing" or "the gateway request scheme". Several minuted items were later corrected or reassigned to other signers. Here is what applied to this scheme on the rollout day:

- **Signed headers:** every header except `authorization` is signed. It was agreed on 2025-12-02 subject to all 5 partner sign-offs by 2025-12-05, and the sign-off register shows all 5 in by 2025-12-04.
- **Header values:** spaces and tabs are trimmed from each end, and runs of spaces or tabs inside are collapsed to one space. This was minuted on 2025-11-04 under the webhook signer, then corrected on 2025-11-11 to say it was for this scheme. The later proposal to also lowercase was declined.
- **Empty body:** the body field is always the SHA-256 of the body bytes, so an empty or missing body hashes the empty string instead of signing `UNSIGNED`. This took effect with SDK 3.2.1, which became generally available on 2025-12-01.
- **End of the string:** no trailing LF after the last field, per the 2025-12-02 decision. This overrides GW-052 in the register.
- **Signed header name list:** names are joined with `;`. The `,` proposal was withdrawn on 2025-11-18, and the 2025-11-25 minute that agreed it was corrected as belonging to internal service signing.
- **Query parameter without `=`:** it is written with a trailing `=`, because the bare-name trial was backed out on 2025-12-02.
- **Ordering:** parameters sort by name only and keep their arrival order within a name.
- **Path:** signed as received. Collapsing dot segments waits for SDK 3.3, which becomes generally available on 2026-01-13.
- **Percent escapes:** signed as they arrive. The uppercasing was conditional on the proxy rewriting escapes, and the capture showed it doesn't.
- **Key id matching:** exact and case-sensitive.

**Keys**

The roster is `gw-prod-01` and `gw-prod-02`, the two key files the legacy signer opened in the strace and lsof. `gw-prod-03` belongs to the export signer, and the notes say moving this scheme onto it is a separate Q1 change. The key file is used whole, with its trailing newline, because the legacy signer read all 33 bytes.

The sample's record 6 carries an `Authorization` header signed with the newline stripped from the key. The pipeline correctly rejects it as `signature-mismatch`. That header looks like a deliberate trap for the webhook signer's key rule.

**Compliance**

Sources contain no network client or network access, and the output is deterministic.
